verdict.rationale: Oneleet's Fieldwork marketing page says its AI agents collect, validate, and package compliance evidence 'on your schedule', which suggests user-scheduled agentic work running in the background. Code Security also runs a fixed daily scan on its own, but that is a built-in schedule rather than an automation the user sets up. Service keys and the MCP server are only building blocks a developer would use to construct automations, so they earn no credit here. Missing for 10: documentation on how to configure, schedule, and monitor autonomous automations; user-defined triggers or workflows beyond evidence collection; any hands-on or independent corroboration of Fieldwork's agents.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: Fieldwork's AI agents collect, validate, and package the evidence – across your enterprise systems, on your schedule.
Oneleet scans the target branch of each repository once a day
